rules.cwe_name: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
rules.description: Tokens used for sensitive tasks, such as, password recovery, and email confirmation, should not use predictable values.

rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Some mathematical operations on random numbers can cause bias in the results and compromise security.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
rules.description: Using a cryptographically weak pseudo-random number generator to generate a security-sensitive value may allow an attacker to predict what value will be generated.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If the id of an HTML attribute is malformed, its interpretation may be browser-dependent.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.
An assignment to a global variable that is never used has no effect.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.
Legacy category for insecure credential creation, storage, validation, or handling.
A security-relevant comparison checks the wrong, incomplete, or non-canonical value.
Legacy category for cryptographic design or implementation weaknesses.
